title: Client
body:
The machine making the request — in web development, almost always the user's browser. It builds the [[HTTP]] request, decides the method, [[URL]], headers and body, sends it, and does something with the response.

The defining property of the client is that **you do not control it**. It belongs to the user, who can open DevTools and read every line of your JavaScript, change any variable, modify or replay any request, and disable any check you wrote. Everything on this side is a suggestion.

That's why the client/server split isn't just about where code physically runs — it's about where trust can live. Presentation, interaction and convenience validation belong on the client; [[Authentication]], [[Authorization]] and anything whose correctness actually matters belong on the [[Server Side]]. See [[Frontend]].
